clues: This seaside town in Devon, England, sits on the north side of a bay. A fishing port lies across that bay from it.
This town is famed for its mild climate, a soft touch for a shore in England. Its mild air earned it the nickname the English Riviera.
At first, work here meant fish and farms, as in many shore towns. In the early 1800s, it grew into a smart, famed beach resort.
Agatha Christie, the famed crime writer, was born in this town. A mile long walk with plaques now tells the tale of her life and work.
A poet with weak health came here in 1837 to heal, on her doctor's advice. Her old home is now part of the Regina Hotel.
